title: Ceramic Omnidirectional Bioprinting in Cell-Laden Suspensions for the Generation of Bone Analogs
protocol: Weigh out calcium hydrogen phosphate (CaHPO4) and calcium carbonate (CaCO3) powders in a 3:2 Ca:P molar ratio.
Thoroughly homogenize the two powders using a spatula.
Add the calcium hydrogen phosphate-calcium carbonate powder mixture to a zirconia crucible such that it is no more than 75% full.
Transfer the crucible to a furnace.
Heat to 1,400 °C at a rate of 5 °C/min and hold for 3 h.
Quench the reaction by removing the crucible from the furnace and leave it atop a refractory block.
Allow the crucible to cool completely before handling.
Use a mortar and pestle to break and grind the α-TCP cake such that the resulting granules have a maximum size of 200 µm.
Further grind the granules using a planetary mill in two stages.
Add 3 mm yttria-stabilized zirconia balls in a weight ratio of 8:1 balls:powder, then 100% ethanol in a weight ratio of 3:1 ethanol:powder.
Secure the lid and grind for 2 h at 180 rpm.
Collect the suspension and separate the balls, using 100% ethanol for washing.
Dry the suspension in an oven at 120 °C for 24 h.
Add the dried powder to milling jars with 1 mm zirconia balls and 100% ethanol in the same weight ratios as in the first stage.
Grind for 2 h at 180 rpm.
Separate the mixture.
Dry the separated material.
Add 2 g of α-TCP powder, 630 µL of glycerol, and 130 µL of polysorbate 80 to a ball mill jar with continuous stirring using a spatula.
Add 100 mg of ammonium phosphate dibasic ((NH4)2HPO4, APD).
Stir to combine the mixture thoroughly.
Load a 25 mm zirconia ball into the jar and secure the lid.
Place the jar in a planetary mill for 60 min at 180 rpm.
Pause halfway through milling to scrape down the sides of the jar with a spatula.
Using a spatula, load the ink into a 1 mL syringe.
Wrap the syringe adequately to avoid contact with moisture.
Store at -20 °C if not used immediately.
Print the bone-ink in deionized water and allow it to set for 5 min.
Wash the sample three times with 100% ethanol.
Allow the washed sample to dry completely.
Coat the dried sample with a thin layer (15 nm thickness) of gold.
Capture micrographs using a field emission scanning electron microscope at an acceleration voltage of 5 kV.
Weigh out 10 g of gelatin type A (porcine, Bloom strength 300) and add it to a conical flask with 90 mL of PBS.
Heat the mixture to 50 °C while stirring until the gelatin is completely dissolved.
Add 5.796 mL of methacrylic anhydride to the solution.
Place a rubber cap on the conical flask and continue stirring in the dark at 50 °C for 90 min.
Quench the reaction by diluting the conical flask's contents twofold with PBS.
Decant into 50 mL tubes and centrifuge at 3,000 × g at room temperature for 3 min to remove unreacted methacrylic anhydride.
Dialyze the supernatant inside 14 kDa cutoff cellulose dialysis tubes against deionized water at 40 °C for 5 days while gently stirring.
Replace the deionized water every day.
Decant into 50 mL tubes and secure the cap.
Place the tube in the refrigerator for 12 h to prepare for storage.
Store in a refrigerator for up to 7 days.
Freeze using liquid nitrogen and immediately lyophilize for 5 days at −54 °C and 0.4 mbar.
Make a 10% w/w GelMA solution in PBS by weighing the lyophilized GelMA, adding it to a tube with PBS, and heating in a water bath at 50 °C until fully hydrated.
Add 37 mL of oil per 1 mL of GelMA solution to a beaker, ensuring it is no more than 65% full.
Set up a double-beaker system on a hot plate with magnetic stirring by placing the beaker containing oil inside a larger beaker.
Heat the mixture to 40 °C while stirring.
Load the GelMA solution into a syringe and add it dropwise into the stirring oil through a 0.45 µm filter.
Allow the emulsion to equilibrate for 10 min.
Reduce the temperature of the emulsion to 15°C by adding crushed ice between the two beakers.
Add acetone to the spinning emulsion in a volume ratio of 1:11 GelMA solution to acetone through a funnel.
Stir for 60 minutes.
Decant the contents of the beaker into 50 mL tubes, washing the walls with acetone.
Leave for 20 minutes to allow dehydrated microgels to settle at the bottom.
Discard the supernatant and wash at least twice with acetone.
Consolidate the washed material into one tube, top up with acetone, and sonicate for 10 seconds.
Wash two more times with acetone.
Store in acetone at room temperature until required for printing.
Prepare a 1% w/w solution of GelMA in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium by weighing lyophilized GelMA into a tube and adding DMEM.
Heat the mixture in a water bath at 50°C until fully hydrated.
Evaporate the acetone from the dehydrated microgels, weigh the resulting powder, and transfer to a sterile environment.
Evaporate the acetone.
Add DMEM, 1% w/w GelMA solution in DMEM, and 2.5% w/w LAP initiator solution to achieve a final packing fraction of 30%.
Allow the mixture to fully hydrate for at least 12 hours at room temperature.
Store the hydrated suspension in a refrigerator for up to 7 days.
Allow the suspension to come up to room temperature before use.
Culture ADSCs in low-glucose DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin-streptomycin at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until confluent.
Remove the medium from the tissue culture flask.
Wash ADSCs with sterile PBS.
Incubate cells with 0.25% trypsin for 3 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Centrifuge cells at 150 × g at room temperature for 5 min to pellet them.
Count the cells and calculate 5 × 10^5 cells for each 1 mL of GelMA microgels.
Allocate the required volume of cell suspension to a separate tube.
Pellet the cells as above in the separate tube.
Carefully remove as much supernatant as possible using a pipette, leaving only the cell pellet.
Add the required volume of microgel suspension to the cell pellet.
Aspirate gently to ensure even distribution of cells within the microgel suspension.
If excess air bubbles are present, centrifuge gently and pipette up and down to redistribute the cells.
Load the cell-laden microgel suspension into a 10 mm x 10 mm x 3 mm reactor with a volume capacity of 100 µL using a pipette.
Deposit bone-ink using a 1 mL syringe fitted with a 23 G needle.
Crosslink the cell- and bone-ink-laden GelMA microgel construct with a UV-crosslinker lamp at 405 nm for 90 seconds.
Transfer the crosslinked construct to an appropriately sized well plate immediately after crosslinking.
Cover the well plate with complete DMEM.
Incubate the constructs at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Replace the culture medium after 24 hours.
Continue replacing the culture medium every 48-72 hours as required.
At each time point, wash the constructs with PBS.
Add a solution of phenol-free DMEM containing 4 mM calcein and 2 mM ethidium bromide.
Incubate for 1 h at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Wash with PBS.
Transfer to a glass-bottomed dish for imaging.
Image using a confocal microscope at Ex/Em spectra of 494/517 nm for calcein.
Image using a confocal microscope at Ex/Em spectra of 528/617 nm for ethidium bromide.
